newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says U.S. stance hindering aviation talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan says U.S. stance hindering aviation talks.

text.p: Aviation talks between the United States and Japan took a step backwards after the U.S. hardened its stance on the first day of formal discussions on Monday, a Japanese government official told reporters.
After agreeing last month to strike a new air deal by the end of September, Japan and the U.S. have begun three days of talks aimed at forging a new aviation accord.

According to the official, the U.S. said it would only recognise an upgrading of rights for All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) if Japan agreed to an open skies arrangement, a U.S.-led policy of a free market without government restrictions on international air travel.

He also said the U.S. had raised its demands for the number of new routes to be given to U.S. carriers with lesser rights under the current treaty, while demanding nearly twice the number of routes mentioned in informal talks earlier this year.
In the past few years, Washington has consistently pressed Japan to accept an open skies arrangement, but Japan has sworn it would never accept one.
Japan has repeatedly said that it supports deregulation but believes that lifting all government restrictions would only lead to alliances dominated by U.S. carriers.
Asked about the Japanese reaction to the new U.S. demands, the official quoted a Japanese negotiator as saying: "It makes your adrenaline dance."
The official added that he expected the remaining negotiations to be quite difficult.
